# IBEx.Fi Integration Widget — AI Quick Rules

Use this quick file first, then read `docs/llms-full.txt` for full implementation details.

## Mandatory API Behavior

- Use `GET/POST /v1.2/auth/sign-in` first, then fallback to `GET/POST /v1.2/auth/sign-up`.
- **Use enriched sign-in** (critical): always pass `includeBalance: true`, `includeTransactions: true`, `includeUserdata: true` in the `POST /v1.2/auth/sign-in` body. The auth response will include all user data — **do not call `GET /users/me` after sign-in**.
- The API has a strict anti-flood guard (`429 Too Many Requests`) that blocks rapid duplicate calls per user. If you call `GET /users/me` right after an enriched sign-in, you waste a request and risk a 429.
- Persist tokens returned by auth immediately (`access_token`, `refresh_token`).
- After auth success, complete session bootstrap atomically before parallel API calls:
  - persist `access_token`, `refresh_token`, resolved `rpId`,
  - set auth headers source for HTTP client/proxy,
  - then run protected calls (`/users/me*`).
- Do not refresh immediately after auth success.
- Access token TTL is typically `expires_in = 3600` (~1 hour).

## Refresh Rules (Critical)

- On `401/403` from authenticated endpoints, run one refresh (`POST /v1.2/auth/refresh`) then retry original request once.
- Use a global single-flight refresh lock so parallel failures share one refresh call.
- Never refresh recursively on refresh route failures.
- If refresh fails (`401/403`), clear session and switch UI state to disconnected.

## Headers and Identity

- Always send both auth headers on protected routes:
  - `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`
  - `X-IBEx-Auth: Bearer <access_token>`
- Send `X-Rp-Id` and `X-RpId` on all requests.
- Apply the same rpId propagation rules to refresh routes (`POST /v1.2/auth/refresh`) in app proxy/session context.
- Extract `externalUserId` from the **auth response `subject` field** (sign-in/sign-up/refresh) — NOT from `GET /users/me`.
  - `GET /users/me` is an aggregated response (sections: `addresses`, `balances`, `kycStatus`, etc.) — `externalUserId` is not at the top level.
  - Fallback: decode the stored JWT `access_token` → `sub` claim.
- Persist `externalUserId` and propagate it in your app session/proxy context for all user-scoped calls.
- Persist normalized user data in local storage scoped by external user (`${externalUserId}_*`) and refresh UI from that cache first, then network.

## Address Book + VoP Clarification

- Use `POST /v1.2/users/me/addressbook` to create contacts.
- For IBAN flow, send `iban` and `respondingPspBic` together.
- Do not call any direct VoP endpoint for this flow.
- VoP is executed internally by the addressbook create endpoint.
- Do not invent demo/test data unless explicitly requested by the developer.
- If demo/test seed is required, reuse only the canonical `FAUCET_*` keys defined in `AGENTS.md` (do not duplicate literal values here).

## Safe Operations (SDK Scope)

- Safe operations use a 2-step flow via `POST/PUT /v1.2/safes/operations`:
  1. **Prepare** (POST): submit operation(s) → receive `credentialRequestOptions` (WebAuthn challenge)
  2. **Execute** (PUT): submit signed `credential` (WebAuthn assertion) → on-chain execution returns `userOpHash`
- Supported operations exposed by SDK:
  - `SIGN_MESSAGE`: EIP-191 personal_sign. Body: `{ type: "SIGN_MESSAGE", message: "<string>" }`
  - `ENABLE_RECOVERY`: activate recovery module on a deployed Safe. Body: `{ type: "ENABLE_RECOVERY", firstName, lastName, birthDate (YYYY-MM-DD), birthCity, birthCountry }`
  - `CANCEL_RECOVERY`: disable previously enabled recovery. Body: `{ type: "CANCEL_RECOVERY" }`
  - `SWAP_FROM_QUOTE`: execute a token swap from a pre-obtained quote. Body: `{ type: "SWAP_FROM_QUOTE", quoteId: "<string>", orderUid?: "<string>" }`
- Required request fields for all safe operations:
  - `safeAddress` (string, required)
  - `operations` (array, required)
  - `chainId` (number, optional)
  - `walletMode` (optional): `"SAFE_4337"` or `"EOA_7702"`
- Safe must be deployed before `ENABLE_RECOVERY` (lazy/undeployed Safes will receive an error).
- Safe must already have recovery enabled before `CANCEL_RECOVERY`.

## Swap Quote (SDK Scope)

- Get a DEX swap quote: `GET /v1.2/safes/swap/quote` with query params:
  - `sellTokenAddress` (required), `buyTokenAddress` (required), `amount` (required, human-readable)
  - `chainId` (optional), `safeAddress` (optional, defaults to user's first Safe), `provider` (optional: `COWSWAP`, `1INCH`, or `BOTH`)
- Response includes `quoteId`, `buyAmount`, `sellAmount`, fee, validity, etc.
- Use the returned `quoteId` with `SWAP_FROM_QUOTE` operation via `POST /v1.2/safes/operations`.
- Full swap flow: `getSwapQuote()` → `swapFromQuote()` → WebAuthn sign → `executeSafeOperations()`.

## SEPA Payments and Mandates (SDK Scope)

- IBAN management:
  - `POST /v1.2/sepa/iban/add`
  - `GET /v1.2/sepa/iban`
- Payment flow (2 steps):
  - `POST /v1.2/sepa/payments` -> create approval intent + passkey challenge
  - `PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments` -> confirm/execute payment with `approvalId` + signed `credential`
- Transactions:
  - `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions`
  - `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id`
- Mandates:
  - `POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates`
  - `GET /v1.2/sepa/mandates`
  - `GET /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id`
  - `PATCH /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/status`
  - `POST /v1.2/sepa/mandates/:id/cancel`
- Keep mandate status lifecycle strict: use `validated | suspended | cancelled`.

## DevTools Topup Endpoints (Test Only)

- For development roundtrip tests, you can use:
  - `POST /api/admin/devtools/sepa/topup`
  - `POST /api/admin/devtools/crypto/topup`
- These are DevTools/admin helpers (not end-user production flows).
- Keep tenant/rpId consistency for the whole test tuple.
- Reuse only canonical `FAUCET_*` keys from `AGENTS.md` (do not duplicate literal faucet values here).

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Example | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `IBEX_API_URL` | `https://passkeys-testnet.ibex.fi` | Base URL of the IBEx API |
| `IBEX_RP_ID` | `localhost` or `demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi` | WebAuthn Relying Party ID — **must match browser hostname** |
| `PORT` | `3001` | Local dev server port |

Copy `env/.env.example` to `env/.env.local` before starting.

## rpId / WebAuthn — CRITICAL CONSTRAINT

**`IBEX_RP_ID` must always equal the hostname in the browser address bar.** This is a browser-level WebAuthn security rule that cannot be bypassed.

### The full auth consistency chain

```
Browser hostname = WebAuthn rpId = JWT issuer = API request rpId (headers)
```

If any link in this chain differs → 401 Unauthorized.

### Valid dev setups

| Browser URL | `IBEX_RP_ID` | Works? |
|-------------|-------------|--------|
| `http://localhost:5173/` | `localhost` | Everything OK (`localhost` is registered on testnet) |
| `http://demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi:5173/` | `demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi` | Everything OK (requires `/etc/hosts`: `127.0.0.1 demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi`) |
| `http://localhost:5173/` | `demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi` | **FAILS** — WebAuthn rejects rpId |

### Forbidden approaches (do not attempt)

- Never set `IBEX_RP_ID` to a domain that differs from the browser hostname
- Never "split" rpId (API headers → one value, WebAuthn → another) — the server verifies both sides
- Never add `VITE_IBEX_RP_ID` or frontend overrides to force a different rpId than the browser hostname
- Users/credentials are namespaced by rpId: `localhost` user ≠ `demobaas-prat1.ibex.fi` user

## Proxy Requirement

- Browser must call your own backend proxy (CORS-safe), not IBEx directly.
- Proxy should forward query params and required headers, and normalize/strip incompatible encoding headers.

## Realtime (When Required)

- WS endpoint is `/ws` on the same API host (optionally `?blockchainId=<id>`).
- Send auth as first WS message within 30s:
  - `{ "type": "auth", "token": "<access_token>", "clientName": "<app>" }`
- Handle close codes correctly:
  - `4001`: auth timeout -> reconnect quickly and auth immediately
  - `4002`: auth failed/expired token -> refresh once, then reconnect
  - `4003`: duplicate active session -> do not auto-reconnect; close old session first
- Handle at least these events:
  - initial/session: `auth_success`, `connection_success`, `user_data`, `balance_data`, `transaction_data`
  - push: `balance_update`, `new_transaction`, `fiat_balance_update`, `fiat_transaction_update`, `user_iban_updated`, `user_ky_updated`
- `user_data` may be sent twice during initial burst; process idempotently and do not rely on strict event ordering.
- If WS is healthy, use WS events as the primary refresh channel for balances/transactions/KY/IBAN updates.
- On prolonged WS failure, fallback to HTTP (`/v1.2/users/me`, `/v1.2/users/me/balances`, `/v1.2/users/me/transactions`).

## Data Paths Quick Tips

- IBANs:
  - HTTP: `users/me -> ibans.ibans[]`
  - WS: `user_data -> data.ibans.data.ibans[]` + signal `user_iban_updated`
- Wallets:
  - HTTP: `users/me -> addresses.wallets[]`
  - WS: `user_data -> data.addresses.data.wallets[]` (`auth_success.data.safeAddress` is only session safe)
- Address book:
  - HTTP: `users/me -> addressbook.data[]`
  - WS snapshot: `user_data -> data.addressbook.data.data[]` (envelope mode)
- Balances:
  - HTTP: `users/me -> balances`
  - WS: `balance_data`, `balance_update`, `fiat_balance_update`
- Transactions:
  - HTTP: `users/me -> transactions`
  - WS: `transaction_data`, `new_transaction`, `fiat_transaction_update`
- CRYPTO transfers:
  - Create transfer intent/execution through Safe operations (`POST/PUT /v1.2/safes/operations`) with transfer operation types.
  - Read transfer history via `GET /v1.2/users/me/transactions` with `scope=crypto` and filters (`walletAddress`, `direction`, `tokenAddress`, `hash`, `page`, `limit`).
  - Realtime transfer updates come from `new_transaction` (and related `balance_update`).
- SEPA payments:
  - 2-step flow: `POST /v1.2/sepa/payments` (approval intent) then `PUT /v1.2/sepa/payments` (passkey confirmation).
  - Payment history/status: `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions` and `GET /v1.2/sepa/transactions/:id`.
  - Realtime status/balance signals: `fiat_transaction_update` and `fiat_balance_update`.

## Chain Capability Gating (SDK Scope)

- SDK method: `getChains()` → `GET /v1.2/chains/` (JWT-protected).
- Returns: `Array<{ id, name, modules: { billing, cowswap, recovery, automation } }>`.
- Do not assume a wallet on a chain implies feature availability on that chain.
- Read user chain context from `getMe()` first, especially:
  - `chainid.defaultChainId`
  - `chainid.chains[].chainId` + attached wallets
- Join `getMe()` chain ids with `getChains()` by `id` to retrieve:
  - chain display name (e.g. `"Gnosis"`)
  - available modules (e.g. `billing`, `cowswap`, `recovery`, `automation`)
- Use `getChains()` to decide whether to show/enable:
  - transfers,
  - recovery,
  - automation,
  - multi-sig.
